notes: Every catalog URL was range-requested on 10.11.2026 (curl -r 0-2047) and the returned bytes checked for an MP3/OGG signature; "verified" = "<status> <content-type> <magic>" (ID3 or MPEG frame sync).
Mood, genre and energy are inferred from source tags, titles and album context. Nothing was auditioned. BPM is filled only where the source states it.

"tracks" meets every hard rule. "tracks_content_id_registered" holds Incompetech picks that satisfy the license rules but are registered with YouTube Content ID by their author; use them only where YouTube is not the target, or with the credit in the description.
Mixkit forbids TV/radio broadcast use; filter on license != "Mixkit" for broadcast work.
redistributable=true means the license allows committing the raw file; Mixkit and Pixabay forbid standalone redistribution.

sources.name: Free Music Archive (FMA)
sources.license: Per track: CC0 1.0, CC BY 3.0/4.0, but also many CC BY-NC / BY-NC-SA / BY-ND tracks
sources.commercial: per track (only CC0 and CC BY tracks qualify)
sources.attribution_required: CC BY tracks: yes; CC0: no
sources.attribution_format: "<Title>" by <Artist>, licensed under CC BY <ver> (<license URL>). Source: <FMA track URL>
sources.api: No public API since about 2019. Scrape HTML: each track row carries data-track-info JSON with fileUrl; license is the creativecommons.org link on the track page.
sources.content_id_risk: low for CC0 artists (HoliznaCC0, Loyalty Freak Music, Komiku, Monplaisir); unknown for CC BY artists
sources.notes: License is per track and mixed even inside one album (Broke For Free Directionless EP has 4 BY-NC and 2 BY tracks). Always read the track page license. Scott Holmes and Audiobinger, both popular here, are BY-NC and excluded.

sources.name: Mixkit
sources.api: No API. Category pages (e.g. /free-stock-music/house/) embed data-audio-player-preview-url-value per track; item page /free-stock-music/item/<id>/. The download modal serves the same file as the preview.
sources.content_id_risk: low: license forbids registering tracks on any rights management service; Mixkit asks claim recipients to email team@mixkit.co
sources.notes: Allowed: web/social video, online ads, podcasts, YouTube. NOT allowed: TV and radio broadcast, CDs/DVDs, video games, remixing into a music-only track. A TV or radio spot needs another source. Owned by Envato. No BPM metadata.

sources.name: Musopen (recordings mirrored on Wikimedia Commons)
sources.license: Public Domain Mark / CC0 for the Musopen Kickstarter orchestral recordings; other Musopen recordings vary (some CC BY-SA or NC)
sources.attribution_format: Optional courtesy: "<Work> by <Composer>, performed by Musopen Symphony Orchestra (public domain, musopen.org)"
sources.api: musopen.org returns 403 to curl and needs an account to download. Use the MediaWiki API on commons.wikimedia.org instead (search "Musopen", prop=imageinfo|videoinfo).
sources.direct_url_pattern: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/<h>/<hh>/<File>/<File>.mp3 (transcoded mp3; the original .flac/.ogg under /commons/<h>/<hh>/<File> returned 429 to scripted clients)
sources.content_id_risk: medium: public-domain classical recordings are often matched by Content ID against label recordings of the same work, even though the recording itself is PD
sources.notes: Good source for inspirational orchestral and Nordic calm (Grieg). Movements are long (4-13 min), so cut a segment. Send a descriptive User-Agent to Wikimedia or you get HTTP 429.

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons (audio)
sources.license: Per file: PD, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA (SA is excluded)
sources.attribution_format: Use the file page "Artist" and "LicenseShortName" from extmetadata
sources.notes: Commons also hosts AI-generated (Suno) "epic" tracks marked CC BY. Their copyright status is unclear, so skip them. Kevin MacLeod mirrors here are listed as CC BY 3.0, but the same Content ID caveat as Incompetech applies.

sources.name: Openverse audio API
sources.license: Aggregator; per-item CC license (filter with license=cc0,by)
sources.commercial: per item (license=cc0,by keeps only commercial-safe, derivative-safe items)
sources.attribution_required: per item; each result includes a ready "attribution" string
sources.api: GET https://api.openverse.org/v1/audio/?q=<q>&license=cc0,by&source=jamendo|freesound|ccmixter|wikimedia_audio&page_size=20. Anonymous access works but is rate-limited; register an OAuth client for more.
sources.notes: Index can be stale: 4 of 9 Jamendo CC BY hits had landing pages returning 404 (track removed by the artist) while the storage file still streamed. Those were dropped. Check the landing page before use.

sources.name: Jamendo
sources.license: Per track; many CC BY-NC-ND. Only CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0 tracks are free for commercial use (SA excluded here)
sources.attribution_format: "<Title>" by <Artist>, licensed under CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Source: https://www.jamendo.com/track/<id>
sources.api: Jamendo API v3 needs a client_id (the public demo id is suspended). Openverse indexes Jamendo without a key.
sources.content_id_risk: low-medium: Jamendo's own Content ID program only accepts All Rights Reserved or CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 tracks, so CC BY tracks are not registered via Jamendo, but an artist may use another distributor
sources.notes: Jamendo landing pages are JS-rendered, so licenses here come from Openverse and were not re-confirmed on the page. Jamendo also sells "Jamendo Licensing" commercial licenses, which can confuse the picture. A CC BY track is commercially usable with credit regardless.

sources.name: Freesound
sources.license: Per sound: CC0, CC BY 4.0/3.0, CC BY-NC (exclude NC)
sources.attribution_format: "<Sound name>" by <user> (https://freesound.org/s/<id>/), licensed under CC BY 4.0
sources.api: APIv2 needs a token for search (401 without). Original downloads need OAuth2. HQ preview mp3s are public CDN files. Openverse indexes Freesound without a key.
sources.notes: Best for trailer hits, braams, risers and short loops, not full tracks. Previews are 128 kbps mp3. Sample-pack style loops sometimes reuse commercial sample libraries, so prefer CC0 uploads from active users.

sources.name: ccMixter
sources.license: Per upload: CC BY 3.0, CC BY-NC 3.0, Sampling+, etc.
sources.commercial: per upload (CC BY only; dig.ccmixter.org has a "free for commercial use" filter)
sources.attribution_format: "<Title>" by <user> (feat. <sources>), ccmixter.org/files/<user>/<id>, licensed under CC BY 3.0
sources.api: Open query API, no key: https://ccmixter.org/api/query?f=json&lic=by&tags=instrumental&limit=N returns files[].download_url
sources.notes: Not used for catalog tracks. Remixes often carry vocals, and the license is the most restrictive of all sampled sources. Tested 10.11.2026: the API works and lic=by filtering returns CC BY 3.0 uploads.

sources.name: Incompetech (Kevin MacLeod)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (paid Standard License for no-credit use)
sources.attribution_format:
"<Title>" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com)
Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
sources.api: Full catalog JSON, no key: https://incompetech.com/music/royalty-free/pieces.json (title, filename, bpm, length, feel, genre id, ISRC) and genre.json (id to name).
sources.content_id_risk: HIGH by the brief's rule: Incompetech now pre-registers its catalog with YouTube Content ID and claims any video whose description lacks the credit. Claims are released within 72 h after you add the credit and dispute.
sources.notes: Best metadata of any source (stated BPM and feel for 1443 pieces). Excluded from "tracks" because of the Content ID registration. 17 verified picks are kept in "tracks_content_id_registered". They are usable on LinkedIn and Vimeo, which do not use Content ID, and on YouTube if the credit text sits in the description.

sources.name: Scott Buckley
sources.attribution_format: "<Track Title>" by Scott Buckley, released under CC-BY 4.0. www.scottbuckley.com.au
sources.redistribution_allowed: ambiguous: CC BY allows it, but the site adds "cannot be resold in isolation, or redistributed/reuploaded to music streaming platforms". Treat as false.
sources.api: No API. Category page /library/category/music/ lists mp3 links. Plain curl gets a ModSecurity 406, so send a browser User-Agent plus Accept: text/html.
sources.content_id_risk: HIGH: "Smart Content ID" via We Are Era Music BV claims videos with no credit in the description
sources.notes: Cinematic and orchestral, high quality. Rejected from the main list for the same Content ID reason as Incompetech. The site also says no-credit uses such as TV ads need a paid license, which is just CC BY restated.

sources.name: Pixabay Music
sources.api: No music endpoint in the Pixabay API. Site search sits behind a Cloudflare challenge (403 to curl). Known CDN file URLs do download directly.
sources.content_id_risk: medium, per track: some contributors register their Pixabay tracks with Content ID. Pixabay provides a per-download license certificate for disputes.
sources.notes: No tracks catalogued, because the search pages cannot be scraped and titles cannot be checked against CDN URLs. Standalone redistribution is forbidden. Usable manually: download in a browser, keep the certificate.

sources.name: Uppbeat
sources.commercial: free plan: no (client work and paid ads need the Business plan)
sources.attribution_required: free plan: yes (per-download credit code in the description)
sources.attribution_format: Per-download credit text generated by Uppbeat
sources.api: None; account and per-download credit codes
sources.content_id_risk: HIGH: catalog is Content ID registered; only safelisted channels or credited videos are cleared
sources.notes: REJECTED: the free tier excludes brand and client work, every download needs an account, and the catalog is Content ID registered.

sources.name: Bensound
sources.commercial: limited; commercial and client use generally needs a paid license
sources.content_id_risk: HIGH: the site asks for your YouTube channel ID "to get your videos cleared automatically", which means the catalog is fingerprinted
sources.notes: REJECTED: Content ID registered, per-download codes, and no stable public file URLs. The /licensing page returned 404 on 10.11.2026.

sources.name: YouTube Audio Library
sources.license: YouTube Audio Library license (some tracks CC BY 4.0)
sources.attribution_format: Per-track text shown in the library
sources.api: None; needs a signed-in YouTube Studio session
sources.notes: REJECTED for this skill: no programmatic access, and Google's docs only clearly cover use in YouTube videos. Third-party guides disagree about LinkedIn or client use.

sources.name: Chosic
sources.license: Aggregator; per track CC BY 3.0/4.0, CC BY-SA, CC0, and artist-specific terms
sources.attribution_format: Per-track credit block on the download page
sources.content_id_risk: medium-high: much of the catalog is Kevin MacLeod, Scott Buckley, Alexander Nakarada and others who run credit-scanning Content ID
sources.notes: Not used. Go to the original artist instead. Many Chosic tracks are CC BY-SA (e.g. Purrple Cat lofi), which this brief excludes.

sources.name: Looperman
sources.license: Looperman loop terms (royalty-free inside your own music productions)
sources.commercial: for use inside your own compositions
sources.api: None; terms explicitly prohibit scrapers, downloaders and automated data extraction
sources.content_id_risk: HIGH: commercial songs built on popular Looperman loops get registered, so the bare loop can match
sources.notes: REJECTED: automated download is forbidden by the terms, the loops are for building music rather than for use as finished background beds, and the Content ID false-match risk is high.
